provenance.summary: Structural translation of published guidelines into machine-evaluable form. Probability weights are clinically reasoned seed values, NOT statistically calibrated. Production use requires Clinical Advisory Board sign-off and outcome-data calibration.
sources: WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) Chart Booklet, 2014 revision
WHO IMCI: Handbook for Outpatient Care (2005) and subsequent updates
Federal Ministry of Health Nigeria — National Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Malaria, 2020 (3rd ed.)
WHO Africa Region — Malaria in Children Under Five (epidemiological brief)
Nigerian Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) — child morbidity data
WHO/UNICEF Pneumonia and Diarrhoea Progress Reports
Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) — measles notifiable disease guidance

redFlags.label: Active or recent convulsions
redFlags.explanation: Seizures in a febrile child suggest cerebral malaria, meningitis, or severe sepsis. Immediate stabilization required.

redFlags.label: Lethargy or unconscious child
redFlags.explanation: An IMCI general danger sign — indicates severe disease until proven otherwise.

redFlags.label: Unable to drink or breastfeed
redFlags.explanation: Risk of rapid deterioration from dehydration and sepsis. IMCI general danger sign.

redFlags.label: Vomiting everything taken
redFlags.explanation: Cannot maintain hydration or oral medications — IMCI general danger sign.

redFlags.label: Severe respiratory distress
redFlags.explanation: Severe pneumonia or sepsis-related respiratory failure — requires immediate oxygen and referral.

redFlags.label: Central cyanosis
redFlags.explanation: Severe hypoxaemia — life-threatening, requires immediate oxygen and resuscitation.

redFlags.label: Severe dehydration
redFlags.explanation: IMCI Plan C — requires IV fluid resuscitation and admission.

redFlags.label: Stridor at rest
redFlags.explanation: Upper airway obstruction — risk of imminent airway compromise.

redFlags.label: Neck stiffness
redFlags.explanation: Strong indicator of meningitis until proven otherwise. Empiric antibiotics + urgent LP indicated.

redFlags.label: Bulging fontanelle (infant)
redFlags.explanation: Suggests raised intracranial pressure / meningitis in an infant.

redFlags.label: SpO2 < 90%
redFlags.explanation: Severe hypoxaemia — life-threatening regardless of cause. Oxygen and referral.

redFlags.label: Hyperpyrexia (≥ 41.0°C)
redFlags.explanation: Risk of febrile-related neurological injury. Aggressive cooling and urgent workup.

redFlags.label: Hypothermia in infant under 3 months
redFlags.explanation: Hypothermia in a young infant is a sepsis danger sign — empiric IV antibiotics indicated.

redFlagOverrideActions: Protect the airway; place in recovery position if unconscious or convulsing.
Give rectal diazepam 0.5 mg/kg (or IV diazepam 0.2 mg/kg) if actively convulsing — per IMCI dosing.
Check blood glucose; treat hypoglycaemia (10% dextrose 5 mL/kg IV) if present.
Establish IV access; start IV fluids if shock or severe dehydration suspected.
Give oxygen if SpO2 < 90% or respiratory distress.
Start empirical IV ceftriaxone if meningitis or sepsis suspected — do not delay for investigations.
Refer immediately to the paediatric emergency unit for inpatient management.

differentials.label: Malaria (uncomplicated or severe)
differentials.baseRationale: Endemic in Nigeria — every fever in a child under 5 is malaria until proven otherwise. Holoendemic transmission means baseline probability is high in any presentation.

modifiers.rationale: Recent travel to a malaria-endemic zone.
Temperature ≥ 39°C — high-grade fever consistent with malaria.
Cough plus fast breathing redirects toward pneumonia.

recommendedActions: Order malaria rapid diagnostic test (RDT) immediately; thick film microscopy if available.
If RDT positive, follow Nigerian FMoH protocol: oral ACT for uncomplicated; IV artesunate for severe.
If RDT unavailable and clinical suspicion is high, start treatment empirically per national protocol.
Reassess in 24 hours; admit if any IMCI danger sign develops.

differentials.label: Pneumonia (community-acquired)
differentials.baseRationale: Pneumonia is a leading cause of under-5 mortality in Nigeria — must be actively excluded in every febrile child with respiratory symptoms.

modifiers.rationale: Fast breathing for age is the cardinal IMCI sign of pneumonia.
Chest indrawing indicates severe pneumonia per IMCI classification.
SpO2 < 94% raises probability of pneumonia with lower respiratory involvement.

recommendedActions: Count respiratory rate over a full 60 seconds (do not estimate).
If fast breathing for age per IMCI: oral amoxicillin at IMCI dosing.
Any chest indrawing or SpO2 < 90%: classify as severe pneumonia → refer + first-dose IM ampicillin/gentamicin + oxygen if available.
Reassess after 48 hours.

differentials.label: Sepsis / serious bacterial infection
differentials.baseRationale: Under-5 sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality. Young infants are particularly high-risk and can present without focal signs.

modifiers.rationale: Infants under 3 months — high sepsis risk, atypical presentation common.
Temperature extremes (hypothermia or high fever) suggest systemic infection.
Poor feeding is a non-specific but important sepsis indicator in young children.

recommendedActions: Obtain IV access; draw blood culture before antibiotics if patient is stable enough.
Start empirical IV ceftriaxone per weight-based dosing (or ampicillin + gentamicin in neonates).
Admit; reassess every 30 minutes until stable.

differentials.label: Meningitis (bacterial)
differentials.baseRationale: Nigeria sits within the African meningitis belt — bacterial meningitis remains a high-mortality differential in febrile children.

modifiers.rationale: Neck stiffness is a hallmark of meningitis.
Bulging fontanelle in an infant suggests raised ICP / meningitis.

recommendedActions: Urgent lumbar puncture if no contraindication (no signs of raised ICP, no shock, no focal neurology).
Empiric IV ceftriaxone + dexamethasone immediately — do not delay for LP results.
Admit to high-dependency or paediatric ICU.

differentials.label: Measles
differentials.baseRationale: Measles remains a notifiable, vaccine-preventable cause of febrile illness in Nigeria with recurrent outbreaks.

modifiers.rationale: Maculopapular rash with cough — classic measles prodrome.
Koplik spots are pathognomonic for measles.
Incomplete vaccination raises measles probability substantially.

recommendedActions: Isolate the child from other patients immediately.
Give vitamin A per WHO/IMCI age-based dosing (100,000 IU for 6-11 mo; 200,000 IU for ≥12 mo).
Notify NCDC — measles is a notifiable disease in Nigeria.
Treat secondary bacterial infections as indicated.

differentials.label: Acute gastroenteritis
differentials.baseRationale: Diarrhoeal disease is a major under-5 morbidity driver in Nigeria, especially in rainy-season clusters.

modifiers.rationale: Diarrhoea present — central feature of gastroenteritis.
Vomiting commonly accompanies viral and bacterial gastroenteritis.

recommendedActions: Assess dehydration severity → IMCI Plan A (no), B (some), or C (severe).
Begin ORS per IMCI plan; IV fluids if Plan C.
Give zinc 10–20 mg daily × 14 days (age-dependent dose).
Counsel on safe water and continued feeding.

differentials.label: Typhoid fever
differentials.baseRationale: Typhoid (Salmonella Typhi) is endemic in Nigeria and a key differential for prolonged fever in children with poor sanitation exposure.
recommendedActions: Blood culture — gold standard; collect before antibiotics if the patient is stable.
If high suspicion and severely unwell: empiric IV ceftriaxone.
Counsel on hand hygiene and safe water at discharge.

differentials.label: Acute otitis media
differentials.baseRationale: Common cause of fever in young children, particularly post-URTI; often missed without otoscopy.

modifiers.rationale: Ear pain or discharge — typical AOM presentation.

recommendedActions: Perform otoscopy to confirm.
Oral amoxicillin per IMCI weight-based dosing.
Safety-net: return if persistent ear discharge for more than 2 weeks.

differentials.label: Viral upper respiratory infection
differentials.baseRationale: Deliberately last — viral URTI must not be the default differential for a Nigerian under-5 with fever. Malaria, pneumonia, and sepsis must be actively excluded first.
recommendedActions: Symptomatic care (antipyretics, fluids).
Explicit safety-net counselling on IMCI danger signs.
Review in 48 hours, or sooner if any red flag appears.

missingInfoChecks.prompt: SpO2 not recorded — please measure with a paediatric pulse oximeter before final triage.
Respiratory rate not recorded but cough is present — count over a full 60 seconds to rule out pneumonia.
Fever duration not recorded — important for differentiating typhoid and prolonged-fever differentials.
